text:
anya: Quick heads-up — onboarding sampleapp (go) started failing sporadically when we enabled parallel pagination. Getting mixed 429/502 during warmup.
jamal: Can you share the minimal repro?
anya: PR runner config: `workers=20`, `page_prefetch=2`. Workload: 10k small docs ingestion. Logs show sequences like:
```
-> worker-7 GET /v1/prefetch?page=12 200
-> worker-3 GET /v1/chat 502
-> worker-3 retry immediate
-> worker-3 GET /v1/chat 429
```
rachel: 502 then immediate retry often leads to 429 due to quota windows. We should ensure retry policy differentiates 5xx vs 429: 5xx get capped retries with increasing backoff, 429 should respect `x-rate-limit-reset` and jitter.
anya: go-sdk currently uses a simple fixed backoff for all errors.
jamal: Suggest change: for 429 read `x-rate-limit-reset` (if present) and sleep for reset+random(100-400) ms. For 5xx do exponential backoff. Also introduce a client-side token bucket that consumes tokens on request creation. Refill rate comes from initial `x-rate-limit-limit` probe or from env var.
rachel: We should also add a sampleapp test that mocks initial limit header low and ensures the client ramps.
anya: I'll open PR with changes and a small note in README. Also adding `SDK_DEBUG_RATE` env to simulate lower quotas for dev testing.
sdk-bot: New issue opened: #1120 "go onboarding: client-side limiter + 429 handling" assigned to @anya.
jamal: Thanks. Also shadows: update the quickstart to warn about concurrent prefetch causing token refresh storms.
anya: Will do. Leaving traces in #eng-sre.
